metaDescription: The best beaches in India, coast by coast: Radhanagar, Palolem, Vagator, Om Beach, Varkala, Tarkarli, Shivrajpur, Rushikonda and Puri, plus Blue Flag beaches.
description: A guide to India's standout individual beaches, coast by coast: Radhanagar and Elephant Beach in the Andamans, Bangaram in Lakshadweep, Palolem, Agonda and Vagator in Goa, Om and Kudle in Gokarna, Varkala and Kovalam in Kerala, Tarkarli and Kashid in Maharashtra, Shivrajpur and Nagoa on the Gujarat coast, and Rushikonda, Puri and Paradise Beach on the east coast, with India's Blue Flag beaches.
dek: Some beaches are worth the trip on their own. These are the ones we would plan a holiday around, grouped by coast.

intro: India's coast has hundreds of beaches, but only some combine clean sand, safe swimming in season, beautiful surroundings and easy enough access. This guide picks out the standouts, from the white sand of the Andamans to cliff-backed coves in Goa and Gokarna and temple beaches on the east coast.

Each entry says what the beach is best for and links to the state guide where you will find nearby beaches, when to go and how to plan. For choosing a place to base your holiday, see best beach destinations in India.
quickAnswer: The best beaches in India include Radhanagar and Elephant Beach on Havelock Island, Bangaram in Lakshadweep, Palolem, Agonda and Vagator in Goa, Om and Kudle in Gokarna, Varkala and Kovalam in Kerala, Tarkarli in Maharashtra, Shivrajpur and Diu's Nagoa on the Gujarat coast, and Rushikonda, Puri's Golden Beach and Paradise Beach on the east coast. Swim only in season and in lifeguarded zones.
takeaways: The Andamans (Radhanagar, Elephant, Laxmanpur) have India's most beautiful beaches.
Goa's Palolem, Agonda and Vagator are the pick of its many beaches.
Blue Flag certification marks beaches that meet international standards for water quality, safety and management.
Beaches on the east coast are wider and flatter; the west coast has more coves and cliffs.
Most beaches are closed to swimming in the monsoon.

items.name: Radhanagar Beach, Havelock Island (Andamans)
body: A long curve of white sand and clear water backed by forest, with lifeguards and Blue Flag certification. Famous for sunsets.

items.name: Elephant Beach, Havelock Island
body: Shallow reef close to shore for snorkelling and sea walks, reached by boat or a forest walk.

items.name: Laxmanpur, Neil Island
body: A wide sunset beach, with a natural rock bridge nearby at low tide.

items.name: Bangaram, Lakshadweep
body: A small uninhabited island encircled by a turquoise lagoon.

items.name: Palolem, south Goa
body: A crescent bay framed by headlands, calm in season, with kayaking and boat trips.

items.name: Agonda, south Goa
body: Long, quiet and uncrowded, with a turtle-nesting stretch protected in season.

items.name: Vagator, north Goa
body: Red cliffs, a sheltered bay and Chapora Fort above for sunset.

items.name: Om beach and Kudle, Gokarna
body: Coves linked by a coastal trail; Om beach is shaped like the Om symbol from above.

items.name: St Mary's Island, Udupi
body: Columnar basalt rocks on a small island reached by boat from Malpe, a National Geological Monument.

items.name: Varkala, Kerala
body: The only beach on the Kerala coast backed by high red cliffs, with cafes along the top.

image.alt: Varkala's red cliffs above the beach
image.caption: Varkala

items.name: Lighthouse beach, Kovalam
body: A crescent below the red-and-white lighthouse, busy and well served.

items.name: Marari, Kerala
body: A quiet fishing-village beach near Alappuzha.

items.name: Tarkarli, Maharashtra
body: Long beach with clear water in season, snorkelling and backwaters behind.

items.name: Kashid, Maharashtra
body: Pale sand and casuarinas, the classic weekend beach from Mumbai.

items.name: Shivrajpur, Gujarat
body: White sand and clear water near Dwarka, with Blue Flag certification.

items.name: Nagoa, Diu
body: A horseshoe-shaped bay with calm water and water sports.

items.name: Rushikonda, Visakhapatnam
body: Golden sand below green hills, with Blue Flag certification and water sports.

items.name: Golden Beach, Puri
body: Puri's certified Blue Flag stretch, with traditional lifeguards and sand art.

items.name: Chandipur, Odisha
body: Where the sea retreats several kilometres at low tide.

items.name: Paradise Beach, Puducherry
body: A sandbar reached by a short boat ride from Chunnambar.

items.name: Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu
body: The Shore Temple stands on the sand; surf schools work the village beach.

items.name: Tajpur, West Bengal
body: A quiet, casuarina-lined beach near Digha.

sections.heading: India's Blue Flag beaches
paras: Blue Flag is an international certification run by the Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE). Beaches must meet a long list of criteria on water quality, environmental management, safety and services, and certification is reviewed every year. India had about 18 certified beaches in 2025, after five Maharashtra beaches were added.

Beaches that have held Blue Flag certification include Shivrajpur (Gujarat), Ghoghla (Diu), Kasarkod and Padubidri (Karnataka), Kappad and Chal (Kerala), Rushikonda (Andhra Pradesh), Golden Beach at Puri and Sunapur (Odisha), Radhanagar (Andamans), Kovalam (Tamil Nadu), Eden (Puducherry), Minicoy Thundi and Kadmat (Lakshadweep), and Shrivardhan, Nagaon, Parnaka, Guhagar and Ladghar (Maharashtra). Because certification is renewed annually, check the current list before travelling.
after: See beach tourism in India for what Blue Flag and other coastal rules mean on the ground.

safety: Swim only at beaches with lifeguards, inside the flagged zone, and never when a red flag is up or during the monsoon.
Many popular beaches, such as Marina in Chennai and Rock Beach in Puducherry, prohibit swimming.
Rip currents are common on long, open beaches; if caught, swim parallel to the shore.
Stay away from rocks and cliff edges, especially in rough weather.
Do not touch coral or take shells from protected areas.

faqs.q: Which is the most beautiful beach in India?
faqs.a: Radhanagar Beach on Havelock Island in the Andamans is widely considered the most beautiful.

faqs.q: Which is the cleanest beach in India?
faqs.a: Blue Flag-certified beaches such as Radhanagar, Shivrajpur, Rushikonda and Puri's Golden Beach meet international standards for cleanliness and management.

faqs.q: How many Blue Flag beaches are there in India?
faqs.a: About 18 as of 2025, after five Maharashtra beaches were added. Certification is renewed every year.

faqs.q: Which is the best beach in Goa?
faqs.a: Palolem and Agonda in the south, and Vagator in the north, are among the best.

faqs.q: Which beaches in India are safe for swimming?
faqs.a: Lifeguarded beaches in season, such as Radhanagar, Calangute, Palolem, Kovalam and Rushikonda, within flagged zones.
